scenes.text: Have you ever wondered why the most fashionable emerald green color in Victorian history was actually a silent killer lurking inside the walls of everyday modern homes?
Back in the nineteenth century, a chemist created an insanely vibrant green dye by mixing copper with deadly toxic arsenic, putting it on dresses, toys, and beautiful luxury wallpaper.
As moisture built up inside damp bedrooms, toxic mold released microscopic poisonous gas directly into the air, slowly causing whole families to breathe themselves to death while sleeping at night.
Doctors took decades to expose this terrifying secret pattern, so tell me, would you ever spend a night in a Victorian room? Comment below and hit follow for more strange history!
